rq3_entries.value: the tool computes confidence intervals and bound-parameter updates, and overlays model output with observed means and uncertainty (PDF pp. 5, 7).
quotes: "Once the value is identified by the user, the corresponding confidence intervals are computed automatically." (p. 5)

"Three versions of the observed data are overlaid with varying luminance to provide the information about the mean value and the confidence intervals." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: the expert selects meaningful targets, adjusts interpretable parameters, checks processed observations, and judges model correspondence (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "First, the user selects the suspected maximum of the observed vertical velocity, where the user places an anchor point." (p. 8)

"Next, the surface temperature is adjusted such that the maxima of both the profile and the observation align, where the IsoTrotting ensures that the profile passes through the anchor point at all times." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: the expert continues choosing anchors and parameter changes and interpreting their effects; the paper reports no competence-based transfer of these responsibilities (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Having estimated these parameters for a selected instance, the user can explore the effects of the model parameters on the quality of the model correspondence." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: one atmospheric-convection model and one competition-day dataset of 78 flight tracks, through repeated expert–researcher sessions over four months (PDF p. 7).

"The dataset consists of 78 flight tracks of pilots that were competing against each other on an agreed-upon course." (p. 7)
"The collaboration was carried out in repeated sessions over the course of four months." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: the case study demonstrates the method and reports qualitative efficiency gains, but the “much more efficient” performance claim has no timed or controlled comparison (PDF pp. 7, 9).
quotes: "The tool was then jointly validated and the model performance was estimated on a provided dataset." (p. 7)
"The IsoTrotting makes this much faster, enables the use of arbitrary pairs of parameters and the filtering criteria is defined by clicking on the diagram." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: meteorological empirical-model analysis and validation (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "In this work, we present a design study for empirical modelling of atmospheric convection in meteorology." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support is used to understand and evaluate the current model rather than to develop user competence (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "This technique enables rapid identification of complex behaviour of empirical models." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: expert_or_professional — the intended users are meteorology domain experts (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Our solution allows the domain expert to analyse an empirical model and compare its results against real-world observations." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: evaluation_or_judgment_gap — regression alone cannot reveal suitability, combined effects, or model behavior needed for validation (PDF pp. 1, 3).
quotes: "It does not provide feedback on the suitability of a given model and the selected metric, nor does it help the scientist understand the model’s behaviour." (p. 1)
"Automatic regression fitting cannot answer the above questions, which is why we involve the expert and support them with an interactive visual parameter space analysis." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the paper reports faster paired-parameter analysis with interactively defined criteria (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "The IsoTrotting makes this much faster, enables the use of arbitrary pairs of parameters and the filtering criteria is defined by clicking on the diagram." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — the tool and model were jointly validated on the supplied data (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "The tool was then jointly validated and the model performance was estimated on a provided dataset." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the interface supports an ordered fitting sequence from case selection through anchored and sensitivity-guided parameter adjustment (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Following the analytical steps derived earlier in Sect. 6.1.1, the user performs a series of steps to obtain a fit of the observed thermal." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — inspection exposes surprising or faulty conditions for expert scrutiny (PDF pp. 6, 8).
quotes: "In this particular case we see two clusters that were incorrectly clustered into a single thermal." (p. 6)
"Performing a thorough check of the parameters, an unexpected result is discovered: the model clearly fits best with no drag." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — the representations and bound value respond immediately to the user’s current parameter action (PDF pp. 5, 7).
quotes: "The bound parameter is automatically recomputed by a numerical solver." (p. 5)
"The view is linked to the parameter controls and the changes in parameters are immediately reflected in the air profile view." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — computational operations and human interpretation jointly produce the analysis (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "In the following sections, we document the key insights that were obtained by the mixed machine-human analysis." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: none_comparator_only — the scaffold’s meaning comes from expert choices, explicit equations, statistical processing, and deterministic search rather than AI-generated semantics (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "In our implementation, we use the binary search algorithm to find the value of the secondary parameter that satisfies the anchor point, but other search methods are possible." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_ai_computational — the support is implemented as conventional interactive visualization software (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "The final application is done in PyQt5 and Matplotlib [14]." (p. 9)

limitations: "Even though the analysis tool helped the domain experts to investigate low altitude atmospheric convection for a single day of observations, there are plans to do a subsequent statistical analysis on a larger dataset to obtain more comprehensive results." (PDF p. 9)
"For example, a meaningful error metric for automatic comparison between the observed and simulated velocity profiles will need to be devised." (PDF p. 9)
"Even then, a fully automatic solution will probably not be feasible and a combination of an automatic analysis and visual exploration will be necessary." (PDF p. 9)
"Fist of all, a one-dimensional model is used that assumes that all the properties inside a thermal are constant and different from the properties outside of the thermal." (PDF p. 9)
"Having the model one-dimensional also means that it does not take into account the transient movement of the thermal." (PDF p. 9)
"The equations also describe a steady state, i.e., not a time-dependent behaviour." (PDF p. 9)
"This is a reasonable assumption, but perhaps an oversimplification and reason why the entrainment analysis yields values of zero." (PDF p. 9)

"Further limitations of the studied empirical model are due to the disregard of the effects of moisture making the results unreliable near the condensation level and above it, in the clouds." (PDF p. 9)
"Limitations of the visualization tool include the possibility to work with only one dataset at a time." (PDF p. 9)
"Loading different data is possible, but no visual support for a comparison across datasets is implemented." (PDF p. 9)
"Similarly, no visual support is devised for comparing models of multiple days." (PDF p. 9)
boundary_conditions: "We note that this method is only suitable for exploring the multivariate parameters of the model, as opposed to complex input objects." (PDF p. 5)

"We consider the IsoTrotting technique as a versatile tool to efficiently explore parameter spaces by making simple restrictions in the output domain and it could possibly be used in other applications, even though it focuses on scalar models only." (PDF p. 9)
"There is a possibility to extend this technique to higher-dimensional mathematical objects, but that is beyond the scope of this work." (PDF p. 9)
